title: add-invocation-contextualizer-and-differential-warmup-metering
author: Anita Kapoor
description: Motivation: Long-tail cold-starts for model invocations degrade p99 latency and increase per-token cost; existing telemetry captures aggregate KV cache warmup rates but lacks per-invocation context to attribute warmup efficacy to prompt shapes, model variant, and routing decisions. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) an Invocation Contextualizer: lightweight trace attachments that record a small, sampled snapshot of invocation signals (prompt fingerprint, sequence-length-bucket, model-variant, routing-hint, prefix-kv-hit-rate) emitted as trace attributes and optionally as a compact telemetry blob; 2) a Differential Warmup Meter: a new metric and meter family that computes warmup effectiveness by comparing early-token latency/cost deltas against expected baselines for similar invocation cohorts. The goal is to make regressions in prefetch/KV caching, model routing, and sequencing visible at cohort granularity and enable targeted alerts and dashboard drilldowns. Implementation summary: - telemetry/tracing/contextualizer.go: new sampler that attaches a 128-byte compressed context blob to sampled traces and exposes a feature-flag controlled pipeline to emit a separate warmup_context telemetry event. The contextualizer samples at an adaptive rate (default 1/200 invocations, auto-scale under high-error conditions) and tags traces with compact labels for later join. - telemetry/metrics/warmup_meter.go: introduces warmup_effectiveness{cohort,model_variant,route} gauge and warmup_delta_histogram histogram (compact reservoir). Provides helper functions for runtime to update meters at token 1-5 window and token 20-25 window to compute a delta. - dashboards/warmup_efficiency_dashboard.json: new Grafana dashboard with three panels: cohort delta waterfall, per-variant warmup CTI (cost-time-index), and RPS-decay comparison to detect warmup regressions after deploys. - api/metrics_schema.yaml: schema additions and new metric descriptors for the warmup meters and contextual events. - docs/observability/warmup.md: explains interpretation, alert suggestions, and sample queries for data-scientist/ops workflows. - tests/integration/warmup_e2e.test: synthetic bench that replays cached vs cold invocation streams; asserts warmup_effectiveness > 0.6 on warmed workloads and verifies contextual payloads attach correctly. - deploy/feature-flags.yaml: adds enable_contextualizer flag (default: false) and warmup_sampler_rate; feature gated to limit rollouts during initial investigation. Commits: - Anita Kapoor: initial implementation of contextualizer and warmup meter (wip) - Anita Kapoor: add dashboard json and metrics schema - Anita Kapoor: tests + feature flag + docs - Anita Kapoor: respond to review comments, add labels and tweak sampler policy Changed areas (high level): - Telemetry: new modules for trace enrichment and metric collection; low-level changes minimized and behind flag. - Observability infra: dashboard and schema additions. - Tests: new deterministic e2e that runs in benchmark-lab CI. Backwards compatibility & safety: - Feature-flagged; contextual payloads are intentionally compact and encrypted at rest if persisted; default off for hosted rollout. - Metric names follow existing naming conventions and include tenant/model labels where available. Review thread (summary): - Diego Morales (comment): "Can the contextualizer avoid adding any PII or prompt text? What compression and redaction guarantees do we have?" Author (reply): "Contextualizer only stores prompt fingerprints (rolling 64-bit hash), token counts, and route/model labels. No raw prompt text is captured. Compression uses lz4 on the small proto and we added redaction hooks in contextualizer.go." - Eli Chen (request): "Need unit coverage for the sampler backoff logic and a guard for high-cardinality labels in the meter." Author (reply): "Added unit tests for sampler backoff and label normalization; warmup_meter normalizes cohort labels with a shingle hash and a max-cardinality guard (see metrics_schema.yaml)." - Sophie Laurent (comment/approve): "Nice visibility. Please ensure alerts default to notify SRE only when warmup_effectiveness drops by >20% and p99 increases >50ms." Author (reply): "Agreed; added suggested alert thresholds to docs and included a sample alert rule in dashboards file metadata." CI summary: - build: passed - unit-tests: passed (coverage: +1.2%) - integration-e2e (benchmark-lab): flaky on first run (timing), re-run passed - lint: passed - perf microbench: baseline comparison included in CI artifact (no regressions) Post-merge notes: - Rollout plan: enable_contextualizer=false by default. Ops will enable for 10% of traffic for tenant-sampled experiments and escalate to 100% after 72h if no anomalies. - Monitoring: dashboards added to shared observability folder; SRE runbook updated with playbook section in docs/observability/warmup.md. - Follow-ups: ENG-2210 add automatic anomaly-driven sampler increase and a lightweight join service to hydrate contextual blobs for long-term analysis. Release notes: "Introduces Invocation Contextualizer (opt-in) and Differential Warmup Metering for cohort-level warmup visibility; includes dashboards and a sample alert guide. Feature is behind a rollout flag."
